title: Positional Encoding — Fixed Waves Mark Many Positions
key_insight: Sinusoidal encodings use waves of different frequencies. Nearby positions have related patterns, while many frequencies help distinguish longer distances.
body:
## Fixed Waves Mark Many Positions

Assigning one learned label to every possible position limits the model to labels it saw. Fixed repeating waves offer a structured alternative.

Sinusoidal encodings use waves of different frequencies. Nearby positions have related patterns, while many frequencies help distinguish longer distances.

Learned position vectors can adapt to the training range. Neither method automatically guarantees strong behavior far beyond that range.
common_mistakes: Position information alphabetically sorts every sentence.

real_world_usage: Language meaning depends on order, and position design affects how models handle lengths beyond training.
